goal_name: Goal 5: Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls
target_name: Target 5.2: Eliminate all forms of violence against all women and girls in the public and private spheres, including trafficking and sexual and other types of exploitation
indicator_name1: Indicator 5.2.1.1: Percentage of women aged 15–49 who believe a husband is justified in hitting or beating his wife for at least one of the following reasons: (1) if she goes out without telling him; (2) if she neglects the children; (3) if she argues with him; (4) if she refuses sexual relations; or (5) if she burns the food
organization_name: National Statistical Committee of the Kyrgyz Republic (Department of Household Statistics)
definitions: The percentage of women aged 15–49 who believe that a husband is justified in hitting or beating his wife for at least one of the five specified reasons.
concepts:
Domestic violence

Gender-based violence

Any act that causes physical, sexual or psychological harm to a woman on the basis of her sex, including violence by a husband or intimate partner that may be justified by social or cultural norms.

Tolerance or acceptance of violence

A social or personal attitude according to which the use of violence is considered acceptable in certain circumstances. In this case, it refers to women who believe that a husband is justified in hitting or beating his wife for one or more of the specified reasons.
rationale_interpretation:
The 2023 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey assessed the attitudes of women aged 15–49 towards wife or partner beating by asking respondents whether they considered a husband or partner justified in hitting or beating his wife or partner in various circumstances.

The purpose of these questions is to measure the extent to which violence is socially accepted in settings where women have a lower social status and where violence may be perceived as a disciplinary measure when a woman does not conform to certain expected gender roles.
quality_assurance: The quality of MICS data is ensured through a comprehensive system of standardized methodology, training, supervision and transparency. This makes the survey a reliable source for analysing social indicators, including indicators related to gender equality and violence.
disaggregation: The data are disaggregated by region, urban and rural areas, age group, level of education, marital status and wealth quintile.
international_comparability: The standardized UNICEF methodology ensures the comparability of data across countries and regions. The methodology includes clear guidelines on sampling, question wording, data collection and data processing.
